sections.h2: Who records deeds and mortgages in Manatee County?
sections.html:
The Manatee County Clerk of the Circuit Court is the Official Recorder, so deeds, mortgages, liens, leases and satisfactions all go to the clerk's Recording department in Bradenton. The staff scans each document, stamps the date and time, adds it to the Official Records and indexes it by name so it can be searched.

Recording takes place at 1115 Manatee Avenue West, Bradenton, FL 34205, which is also the address for overnight mail. Regular mail goes to Attn: Recording, P.O. Box 25400, Bradenton, FL 34206. The department's phone is 941-741-4045.

Under s. 28.222 the clerk files deeds, mortgages, claims of lien, lis pendens notices, judgments, military discharge certificates and any other instrument the law requires or allows to be recorded. A seller will mostly care about three groups: the deed that proves title, the mortgage and satisfaction history, and any lien or judgment that could block a closing.

sections.h2: How do you record a document in Manatee County?
sections.html:
There are three ways: bring the original in person, mail it with fees and a self-addressed envelope, or submit it electronically through an approved e-recording vendor. A mailed document is recorded the day it arrives, and the clerk asks for 3 to 5 business days after that for its return.

  • In person: originals come back the same day.
  • By mail: enclose the correct fee and a return envelope; checks are payable to Clerk of Circuit Court.
  • E-recording: you keep the original and the recorded image is sent back once recorded. Deeds, mortgages, assignments and satisfactions are the common e-recorded types.

The clerk cannot supply legal forms or help fill them out, and recommends a real estate attorney or title company. Florida requires a conveyance of land to be in writing and signed in front of two witnesses under s. 689.01, so a deed prepared without those formalities can be rejected or challenged. A change to an existing deed, such as adding or removing a name or moving property into a trust or LLC, needs a new deed recorded.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Manatee County?
sections.html:
The clerk's schedule for a typical instrument works out to $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page, based on figures the clerk prints for a Notice of Commencement. That matches the state charges in s. 28.24: a $5.00 first page and $4.00 each added page, plus a $1.00 and $0.50 modernization charge and a $4 per page technology charge.

An extra $1.00 applies for each name beyond four, under s. 28.24(13). Use the clerk's recording fee calculator for your exact page count. Military discharge (DD-214) recordings are free to the veteran because the county veterans services office is billed.

sections.h2: Who pays document stamp tax on a Manatee County deed?
sections.html:
Every party to the document is liable, whichever side agrees to pay, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Manatee County uses the standard Florida rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, or portion of $100, that every county except Miami-Dade charges.

Consideration includes money, the discharge of an obligation and any mortgage or encumbrance, whether or not the buyer assumes it. The Department of Revenue lists warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds, plus deeds in lieu of foreclosure, as taxable. It says there is no specific exemption for estate planning transfers, though a personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable.

The clerk directs questions on whether the tax is due to the Department of Revenue at 850-488-6800. Spousal homestead deeds where the only consideration is a mortgage, and deeds in a divorce for the marital home, are exempt under s. 201.02(7).

sections.h2: How do you search Manatee County Official Records?
sections.html:
Use the free Official Records search on the clerk's website, where you can print a copy of your deed or a satisfaction for free. A certified copy costs $1.00 a page plus $2.00 for certification and is ordered through the Public Access department at 941-741-4040.

Records go back to the 1850s, and documents recorded before 1978 are held in the Historical Records Library at 941-741-4070. Plat maps as far back as 1887 can be viewed through the clerk's plat search. Land surveys are not recorded with the clerk, so ask the surveyor or the mortgage holder.

  • Not shown on public websites under s. 28.2221: military discharges, death certificates, and family, juvenile and probate case documents.
  • Death certificates and family, juvenile and probate documents can be viewed after registering a free account.
  • Military discharges are not viewable online, and only the person named may buy copies.

The clerk also offers a free Property Alert that emails you when a document matching your registered name is recorded. That is a cheap way for an owner to catch a surprise lien or a fraudulent deed.

sections.h2: What should a Manatee County seller check in the records before listing?
sections.html:
Check that the mortgage you paid off shows a recorded satisfaction, that no lien or judgment is recorded against your name, and that the deed in your chain of title is complete. The clerk says a lender should record a satisfaction or release after payoff, and a copy is available once it is recorded.

Most buyers receive the original deed at closing from the seller or the title company, and an owner who cannot find theirs can request a recorded copy from the clerk. Wills may be filed only after death, through the Probate department at 941-741-4025, which matters for an inherited Manatee County house.

If you are establishing Florida residency for homestead, the Declaration of Domicile can be recorded with the clerk, but the homestead exemption itself is applied for with the Property Appraiser at ManateePAO.gov or 941-748-8208. Florida's deadline for exemption applications is March 1.

sections.h2: What does Manatee County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Manatee County had an estimated 468,200 residents on July 1, 2025, a 17.1 percent rise over the April 2020 base, across 743 square miles of land.

The Census Bureau counts 243,784 housing units, a 74.3 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $391,400, a median gross rent of $1,671 and median household income of $78,457 for 2020 to 2024. About 29.4 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 2025 building permits totaled 11,015. Rapid growth means recording volume is high and recorded chains of title can be long, so ordering a title search early saves days at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Manatee County?
faqs.a: At the Clerk of the Circuit Court's Recording department, 1115 Manatee Avenue West, Bradenton, by mail to P.O. Box 25400, or through an approved e-recording vendor. Call 941-741-4045 with questions.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a document in Manatee County?
faqs.a: The clerk prints $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page for a standard instrument, plus document stamp tax where it applies. Use the clerk's fee calculator for exact totals.

faqs.q: How long are Manatee County records kept online?
faqs.a: Records date to the 1850s, and documents recorded before 1978 are kept in the Historical Records Library. Some record types, such as military discharges and death certificates, are not shown on public websites.

faqs.q: Can the clerk fix a mistake on my recorded deed?
faqs.a: Not by editing it. A new deed has to be prepared and recorded to add or remove names, correct an error or move property into a trust or LLC, and the clerk cannot give legal advice.

faqs.q: Do I pay document stamp tax when I sell in Manatee County?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration on a deed, and all parties are liable, though buyer and seller typically agree who pays at closing.
